title: customer-voices-sprint-synthesis-apr-2029
summary: This sprint capture condenses ~14 customer conversations (CSM calls, support threads, and product trials) and surfaces five near-term product levers that repeatedly appear in asks. The goal is to produce a compact set of actionable proposals the Optimize and Hosted API product teams can evaluate during the May planning cycle. Key emphasis areas: clearer per-route economics, KV/prefix cache controls, deterministic fallback behavior during capacity constraints, embedding throughput tuning for high-QPS use cases, and smoother private deployment upgrades. Customers range from AI startups running multi-tenant apps to regulated enterprises with on-prem inference needs.
high_priority_asks: per-route cost & latency breakdowns in Console (token-level + model variant) - customers need line-item visibility
expose kv-prefix cache controls (pin, invalidate, size & ttl) via API and Console
deterministic fallback policies for model variants during overload (policy editor + dry-run)
adaptive embedding batch tuning and retry visibility for high-QPS embedding endpoints
zero-downtime private deploy upgrade flow and clearer rollback audit trail
problem_patterns: opaque cost spikes linked to batching changes or model rollouts
unexpected semantic regressions after automated optimizer recommendations
embedding throughput drops under burst traffic; retries obscure root cause
customers manually implement prefix-caching at app-layer due to limited native controls
upgrade/rollback uncertainty for Private customers causing windows of elevated latency
raw_customer_quotes: We saw a 2x bill increase the day the model autoscaler kicked in; can't explain it from our side
The model change made completions less consistent — we had to revert, but rollback took forever
Embedding calls used to be steady but now we see 500ms tail latency at peak — retries pile up
If KV cache had a pin/invalidate API we could avoid duplicating prefixes in application code
For our on-prem deployment, upgrades feel like an all-or-nothing event — we want canaries
proposed_solution_candidates: Console change: add 'per-route economics' tab (UI + backend billing mapping) - owner: Jordan, effort: M
API + Console: KV cache control surface (pin, unpin, ttl, size) with metrics - owner: Lin, effort: L
Policy editor for deterministic fallback (canary dry-run, priority rules) - owner: Diego, effort: M
Embedding endpoint: auto-tuner that suggests batch sizes + expose retry diagnostics in logs - owner: Priya, effort: M
Private deploy: staged upgrade workflow + audit-log export for rollbacks - owner: Infra team, effort: L
impact_estimates: Per-route economics tab -> reduces support-cost triage time by ~40% and accelerates customer troubleshooting
KV cache controls -> could cut per-token bill by 8-20% for prompt-heavy workloads that reuse prefixes
Deterministic fallback policy -> decreases downtime surface for capacity events and reduces user-visible errors by ~60%
Embedding tuner -> improves 99th percentile latency for high-QPS customers by ~20% and reduces retries
Private staged upgrades -> increases confidence for enterprise rollouts and reduces emergency support pages by ~70%
open_questions: What SLA class should per-route economics be calculated under (realtime streaming vs batch jobs)?
How much control do we want to expose for KV eviction vs autosizing (safety guardrails vs power users)?
Can fallback policies be implemented without increasing control-plane latency during request routing?
What telemetry will be required to meaningfully recommend embedding batch sizes across varied hardware?
Are there compliance constraints for staged private upgrades that affect audit-log retention windows?
next_actions: Jordan: prototype per-route economics UI mockups and wire to billing sample dataset - due 2029-05-03
Lin: spike for KV control API with a small experiment on dev cluster and perf baselines - due 2029-04-20
Diego: draft fallback policy spec and failure-mode matrix, review with SRE - due 2029-04-24
Priya: collect 3 customer embedding workloads and run auto-tune simulation to estimate gains - due 2029-04-26
Asha: compile final recommendation doc for PM review and tag for May planning - due 2029-05-01
notes: This doc prioritizes repeatable asks surfaced across accounts rather than one-off feature requests. Several customers suggested small UI affordances (per-route filters, quick pin buttons) that combined with backend controls would improve adoption. Recommend pairing engineering spikes with CSM-led beta cohorts to validate impact before broad rollout. Refer to OPT-4123 for initial tracking and tag customers consenting to beta in the Jira ticket.
audience: product, engineering optimize, hosted-api, customer-success, infra
